statements.markdown:
First consider a gap $(a,b)$ with both endpoints in $S$, allowing
$a=0$. Compact-strip regularity gives continuity of $q'$ on $[a,b]$,
even if $\gamma$ jumps at an endpoint. Contact gives
$$
q(a)=a,\qquad q(b)=b,\qquad q'(a),q'(b)\le1.
\tag{5.4}
$$
If the constant coefficient is $c>0$, Section 4 makes $q'$ strictly
convex in the gap. Continuity extends the chord comparison to its
endpoints, giving
$$
q'(t)<\frac{b-t}{b-a}q'(a)+\frac{t-a}{b-a}q'(b)\le1,
\qquad a<t<b.
\tag{5.5}
$$
Integrating contradicts $q(b)-q(a)=b-a$. Equivalently, the mean value
theorem applied to (5.4) requires an interior point with $q'=1$,
whereas (5.5) excludes every such point. The endpoint derivatives need
only be at most one.
statements.section: 5. Excluding terminal, interior and initial gaps

statements.markdown:
Suppose first that $(\ell,r)$ is a support gap with endpoints in $S$
and $r<1$. The coefficient is a positive constant there, because
support at $\ell$ and the absence of mass immediately to its right
force $\mu_\gamma([0,\ell])>0$. Strict convexity of $q'$ and (2) give
$$
q'(t)<\frac{r-t}{r-\ell}q'(\ell)
       +\frac{t-\ell}{r-\ell}q'(r)\leq1
\qquad(\ell<t<r).
$$
Integrating contradicts $q(r)-q(\ell)=r-\ell$, so the geometric
obstruction is an area deficit under $q'$.
statements.section: 2. Contact conditions and the exclusion of gaps

First suppose $(r,s)$ has both endpoints in the support, with
$0\le r<s<1$. Its constant height $c$ is necessarily positive:
for $t$ inside the gap, a small relative neighbourhood of $r$ lies in
$[0,t]$ and has positive mass, so that $c=\mu_\gamma([0,t])>0$.
If $r=0$, this mass is an atom at zero. Contact imposes

$$
q(r)=r,\quad q(s)=s,\quad q'(r)\le1,\quad q'(s)\le1.
$$

\qquad(r<t<s).

statements.markdown:
The support is relatively closed in $[0,1)$. Its complement is a union
of relative open intervals, and the Stieltjes measure vanishes on each
such interval. For $x<y$ in one interval,
$$
\gamma(y)-\gamma(x)=\mu_\gamma((x,y])=0,
$$
so $\gamma$ is constant there.
